paper.title_en: Every three-qubit pure state admits an equal-modulus expansion in a fixed GHZ basis under local unitaries
paper.abstract_en: In general, local unitary transformations alone do not necessarily generate a complete orthonormal basis from a pure state. We prove that any three-qubit pure state, after suitable local unitary transformations, can be expanded in the same fixed Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger basis, and all expansion coefficients have equal modulus. Thus, eight mutually commuting product reflection operators can generate a complete orthonormal basis from an arbitrary three-qubit pure state, thereby proving the three-qubit commuting-reflection encoding conjecture. We also give two applications of this result: first, using three Bell entanglement links, a pre-specified three-qubit pure state can be deterministically distributed through joint projective measurement and local correction; second, using local random unitary operations, a known pure state can be transformed into a maximally mixed state. The mixing protocol uses a shared three-bit classical label and attains the minimum possible label entropy, even when global unitaries are allowed.
